statements.statement: For the deterministic regime bandwidth \(h_n\), the truncated oracle representer obeys \[m^{-1/2}+h_n^{s+1}+n^{-1/2}\left\|r\mathbf 1\{X\ge h_n\}\right\|_{L^2(P_S)}\asymp m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s).\] Thus the exact boundary-bias and oracle source-standard-deviation balance has the regular, critical, and nonregular rates in \(\mathrm{def:frontier\text{-}rate}\).

sampling_model.design: At each triangular-array index \((n,m)\), the observed law is \(\mathbb P_{n,m}=P_S^{\otimes n}\otimes P_T^{\otimes m}\), induced by full-data laws \(F^S_{n,m}\) and \(F^T_{n,m}\) through the projections \(\pi_S\) and \(\pi_T\). The condition \(m/n\to\kappa\) applies only to theorem sequences.
sampling_model.units: Source full-data units are \(W^S=(X,A,Y^S(0),Y^S(1))\) and are observed as \(O^S=\pi_S(W^S)=(X,A,Y)\); target full-data units are \(W^T=(X^T,Y^T(0),Y^T(1))\) and are observed only as \(X^T=\pi_T(W^T)\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary source treatment has known probability \(e(X)\in[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\).
sampling_model.overlap: The source density is \(f_S(x)=x^ag_S(x)\), where \(c_{S,-}\le g_S\le c_{S,+}\) and \(0<c_{S,-}\le a+1\le c_{S,+}\); the target density is \(f_T(x)=g_T(x)\), where \(c_{T,-}\le g_T\le c_{T,+}\) and \(0<c_{T,-}\le1\le c_{T,+}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Under the separate primitive conditions \(t>1/2\) for the one-dimensional density-ratio calibration sieve and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\) for the nuisance-product remainder, deterministic five-fold regression uses ridge-regularized order-\(p\) boundary local polynomials and degree-\(q\) interior B-splines. Interior weights solve the squared-distance semi-unbalanced entropic program with schedules \(\eta_n=\eta_0\), \(\lambda_n=\lambda_0\), \(\xi_n=n^2\), equally spaced knots, and \(J_n=\lceil h_n^{-1}\rceil\); normalized dual potentials give a measurable exponential extension evaluated on held-out source covariates. Inference uses the displayed fold-centered source and target multiplier process and the displayed target, interior-source, boundary-source, and source-covariance variance terms.

estimand_functional: \(\tau=\mathbb E_{P_T}[\mu(X)]=\int_0^1\{\mu_1(x)-\mu_0(x)\}f_T(x)\,dx\), targeted by the unchanged \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\) using the capped downstream RiCOT weight. Here \(J_{\mu,n}\) and \(J_{r,n}\) count regression and calibration knot intervals, giving \(J_{\mu,n}+q\) regression coefficients and a \(J_{r,n}+q\)-dimensional calibration spline space with \(J_{r,n}+q-1\) explicit nonconstant equations. Conditional on the covariates, the estimator has the exact observable expansion \(\sum_i\Gamma_i Z_i\), which yields a finite-sample Hoeffding execution certificate with realized radius \(B_X+R_S+R_T\). The proved rate result is the one-sided minimax lower phase diagram with its matching truncated-oracle envelope; held-out capped-weight localization, empirical frontier attainment, and a frontier-order expected-length guarantee remain open.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their target-outcome estimand and bounded-overlap RiCOT theory inform the unchanged transport kernel, but do not provide polynomial-boundary held-out localization for the capped continuation used here.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The present note preserves their optimization motivation and proves only an observable finite-sample execution certificate for its distinct covariate-only target functional.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Inverse-weighted parameters can be irregular and slower than parametric under arbitrarily large weights.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The source-only lower phase diagram gives the explicit polynomial-boundary exponents and critical logarithm for this transported causal mean.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their minimax moment-estimation result is stated for a uniformly bounded likelihood-ratio class and a different observation model.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: It informs the converse comparison but is not claimed as a nested or matched theorem.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Folded-normal critical values deliver honest fixed-class local-polynomial intervals under their regression conditions.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The corrected interval instead uses a direct bounded-outcome Hoeffding certificate and claims no optimal or frontier-order expected length.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: A bandwidth-indexed Gaussian-process critical value restores coverage after inspecting multiple bandwidths.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The present fixed-bandwidth certificate does not claim data-driven bandwidth adaptation.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their Theorem 1 gives Gaussian or infinitely divisible limits for a one-sample trimmed inverse-probability-weighted mean under regular variation, while Theorem 3 validates local-polynomial trimming-bias correction under differentiability and explicit bandwidth and trimming conditions.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Those inference and trimming-bias results motivate boundary repair but do not give the present two-sample transported fixed-Hölder boundary minimax modulus or critical multiscale logarithm.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their Propositions 3.1--3.2 give alpha-stable limits for one-sample inverse-probability-weighted and doubly robust average-treatment-effect estimators under regular variation, and Theorem 4.1 gives the self-normalized limit used for modified resampling inference.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Those stable-limit and resampling phenomena are distinct from the two-sample transported boundary lower phase diagram proved here.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their Proposition 1 relates overlap-weighted estimands along a tuning path by a Taylor polynomial with a remainder, and Theorem 1 proves root-sample-size asymptotic normality under an exact polynomial-path condition.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: That estimand-path extrapolation condition is different from the fixed-Hölder boundary remainder and minimax lower modulus studied here.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Between-class and ordered moduli govern adaptive confidence intervals for linear functionals.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The nonadaptation theorem is retained, while no executable positive adaptive interval is claimed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Self-similarity supports honest adaptation in the Hölder confidence-band settings studied there.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Self-similarity remains an explicit restriction for a future executable adaptive construction, not a proved adaptive result here.

tldr: A randomized trial may contain progressively fewer patients near a clinically important covariate boundary even when the real-world target population retains positive mass there. In the full-data triangular-array model, the causal target is identified as the observed-law integral \(\tau=\int_0^1\{\mu_1(x)-\mu_0(x)\}f_T(x)\,dx\). The source contribution to root mean-squared error is \(n^{-1/2}\) below the square-integrability threshold \(a=1\), becomes \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\) at the threshold, and is \(n^{-(s+1)/(2s+a+1)}\) above it, in addition to the independent target-sample term \(m^{-1/2}\). Under the separate conditions \(t>1/2\) for the one-dimensional density-ratio calibration sieve and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\) for the nuisance-product remainder, a fully specified squared-distance Riesz-calibrated semi-unbalanced transport program is truncated to the overlap interior and spliced to a deterministic boundary local polynomial. Matching bump and multiscale lower bounds, a fully evaluable fixed-Hölder-class interval with a \(2M\) bias envelope and explicit foldwise multiplier and covariance terms, and a nonadaptation theorem complete the fixed-class program; honest joint adaptation is posed only on an explicit boundary self-similar subclass.

project_justification.gap: Regular Riesz-calibrated transport theory assumes enough overlap for a square-integrable representer, whereas irregular inverse-weight theory does not compute the sharp two-sample Hölder boundary frontier or its critical logarithm.
project_justification.niche: Polynomial trial depletion with a positive target boundary density creates an estimable causal mean whose information geometry changes exactly at \(a=1\); the target sample also imposes a separate parametric floor.
project_justification.fill: Under the separate primitive requirements \(t>1/2\) for density-ratio sieve calibration and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\) for the nuisance-product remainder, the project derives the matching modulus, derives optimizer stability for an executable calibrated-transport plus local-polynomial estimator, and provides fixed-class honest intervals with a fold-centered joint calibration--boundary multiplier envelope and an explicit covariance-complete standard error while making the self-similarity requirement for adaptation explicit.

related_work: Burman et al. (2026) are the optimization and application anchor, not a nested estimand comparator. Their target unit contains an observed outcome. Proposition 2.1 on page 6 identifies \(\tau_Q=\mathbb E_Q[Y^Q]-\mathbb E_Q[\mu_0(X^Q)]\), while Theorem 3.1 on pages 6--7 gives its efficient influence function; this core instead observes only target covariates and targets \(\mathbb E_{P_T}[\mu_1(X)-\mu_0(X)]\). Their Assumption 1(iv) on page 7 imposes bounded target-to-trial density ratio, Theorem 4.5 on pages 13--14 proves calibrated-weight consistency, Theorem 5.2 on page 16 gives efficient inference for their estimand, and Section 8 on pages 23--24 studies 30-month mortality in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy. Section S4.3 is the source locator for the standard one-dimensional density-ratio calibration-sieve threshold \(t>1/2\). That threshold is separate from \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), which controls the distinct nuisance-product remainder. The present transport program is informed by their semi-unbalanced entropic geometry without claiming that its \(a=0\) case reproduces their theorem. Khan and Tamer (2010) establish the general connection between arbitrarily large inverse weights and slower-than-parametric estimation, but do not analyze a two-sample transported Hölder functional. Zhang et al. (2025) define the uniformly bounded likelihood-ratio class \(\mathcal V\) in Section 1 on page 2 and state its minimax lower bound as Theorem 1 in Appendix A.1 on page 12. Their observation model and Sobolev moment class differ, so their result informs the calibration and lower-bound comparison rather than being claimed as a theorem-level extension. Donoho (1994) supplies the modulus-of-continuity and affine-recovery blueprint used to turn the weighted boundary geometry into a minimax theorem. Ma and Wang (2020) show how local polynomial correction repairs trimming bias and how weak overlap changes limit laws; the present first proof step is instead a joint interior Riesz-calibration and target empirical process. Orihara, Komukai, and Li (2026) extrapolate a path of overlap-weighted estimands, but their key polynomial approximation condition is not the fixed-Hölder boundary remainder controlled here. Armstrong and Kolesár (2020) supply the fixed-class folded-normal critical value, while Armstrong and Kolesár (2018) explain the extra correction required after inspecting multiple scales. Cai and Low (2004) provide the ordered-modulus language for nonadaptation, and Bull (2012) supplies the multiscale self-similarity mechanism adapted in the open question.
technical_internal_limitation: The critical lower bound cannot follow from one boundary bump: a single bump at \(a=1\) yields only \(n^{-1/2}\). The \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\) claim therefore stands or falls with a multiscale mixture whose likelihood divergence remains bounded while separations accumulate across scales. On the upper side, the convex-program stability, maximum-leverage control, spline calibration residual, boundary bias, target empirical noise, conditional multiplier approximation, and studentization must all be proved jointly from the primitive class. The primitive restrictions \(t>1/2\) for density-ratio sieve calibration and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\) for the nuisance-product remainder are maintained separately; neither assumes a fitted-weight rate, optimizer stability, calibration rate, or normal approximation.
honest_scope: The fixed-class statements cover a one-dimensional boundary, known randomized-treatment propensity, bounded outcomes, the standard threshold \(t>1/2\) for the one-dimensional density-ratio calibration sieve, the separate product-smoothness relation \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\) for the nuisance-product remainder, fixed transport penalties, and prespecified \((a,s,t,M)\). Each finite-\((n,m)\) minimax class is independent of the asymptotic balance condition; \(m/n\to\kappa\) is imposed only on theorem sequences. Within this covariate-only target model, \(a=0\) reduces to bounded-ratio regular two-sample transport and \(0<a<1\) permits unbounded but square-integrable weights at the same root rate. This reduction is not a specialization of Burman et al.'s target-outcome estimand. No unrestricted adaptive interval is claimed. Joint adaptation to \(a\) and \(s\) is confined to the explicit self-similar class and remains the first-class open-ended question. Multivariate boundary manifolds, observational treatment assignment, and formal sensitivity analysis for transportability are outside this core.
